Applying the mean value theorem for the integrals, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(b-a)f(c) & ={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ f(c) & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ f(c) & =\frac{1}{4-1}{\int }_{1}^{4}(2{x}^{2}+3)\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{1}{3}\cdot (\frac{2}{3}{x}^{3}+3x)|}_{1}^{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[(\frac{2}{3}\cdot {4}^{3}+3\cdot 4)-(\frac{2}{3}\cdot {1}^{3}+3\cdot 1)] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(\frac{164}{3}-\frac{11}{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(51) \\  & =17.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the expression for $f(x)$ to solve for the value of $c:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(c) & =17 \\ 2{c}^{2}+3 & =17 \\ 2{c}^{2} & =14 \\ {c}^{2} & =7 \\ c & =\pm \sqrt{7}\end{aligned}
$$

However, since $c\in [1,4],$ we take only $c=\sqrt{7}.$
